Definition: An audible statement helps an older adult understand whether the agent is addressing them or involving family.
Sub-theme: Older adults respond before family is involved
Theme: Older adults accept family involvement when they stay in control
Example quote: When it said it is working for me, I understood it better. (P10, Phase 2, L13)
Reflexivity note: Spoken Bangla role announcements were deployed; unfamiliarity tempers the positive account.

Definition: A request marks the moment when a private reminder can become shared care work.
Sub-theme: Older adults respond before family is involved
Theme: Older adults accept family involvement when they stay in control
Example quote: Then later it asked for permission to involve the family [...] I agreed. (P10, Phase 2, L21)
Reflexivity note: The request and grant prompt was deployed in this self reported episode.

Definition: Older adults stop unnecessary family involvement when they report that the dose was already taken.
Sub-theme: Older adults respond before family is involved
Theme: Older adults accept family involvement when they stay in control
Example quote: Then I stopped the family alert because there was no need to worry them. (P10, Phase 2, L31)
Reflexivity note: No app log verifies how often participants declined.

Definition: The medicine taker expects an opportunity to respond before the agent contacts another person.
Sub-theme: Older adults respond before family is involved
Theme: Older adults accept family involvement when they stay in control
Example quote: First remind me. Give me a chance to respond. Then family can be told. (P05, Phase 2, L155)
Reflexivity note: This order was elicited but recurs across accounts.

Definition: Another reminder and waiting period should precede a handoff to the care network.
Sub-theme: Older adults respond before family is involved
Theme: Older adults accept family involvement when they stay in control
Example quote: Give me the reminder first. Then maybe another reminder. (P11, Phase 2, L128)
Reflexivity note: Risk graded escalation was not implemented.

Definition: An unresolved event goes to a selected caregiver rather than the entire household.
Sub-theme: Older adults respond before family is involved
Theme: Older adults accept family involvement when they stay in control
Example quote: One family member is enough. If everyone gets it, then everybody may start asking me. (P13, Phase 2, L130)
Reflexivity note: This hypothetical boundary protects selective involvement.

Definition: Successful doses and small delays do not justify continuous family notification.
Sub-theme: Older adults respond before family is involved
Theme: Older adults accept family involvement when they stay in control
Example quote: normal medicine reminders should remain with me. (P17, Phase 2, L126)
Reflexivity note: This self manager prevents collectivism from becoming compulsory disclosure.

Definition: An older adult may take medicine without pressing the confirmation control.
Sub-theme: A missing response does not prove a missed dose
Theme: The agent helps when it supports routines and shows uncertainty
Example quote: I had actually taken it, I just forgot the phone part. (P05, Phase 2, L19)
Reflexivity note: This lived record gap limits automatic escalation.

Definition: Work, conversation, travel, delay, or an unheard prompt can produce nonresponse.
Sub-theme: A missing response does not prove a missed dose
Theme: The agent helps when it supports routines and shows uncertainty
Example quote: Silence does not necessarily mean I have forgotten. Sometimes I am simply busy. (P11, Phase 2, L48)
Reflexivity note: Patterned silence interpretation was not deployed.

Definition: An unconfirmed dose should prompt inquiry rather than an immediate missed dose claim.
Sub-theme: A missing response does not prove a missed dose
Theme: The agent helps when it supports routines and shows uncertainty
Example quote: the family should check instead of assuming. (P14, Phase 2, L57)
Reflexivity note: This is an elicited response to record uncertainty.

Definition: Incorrect missed dose implications create avoidable concern and repeated questioning.
Sub-theme: A missing response does not prove a missed dose
Theme: The agent helps when it supports routines and shows uncertainty
Example quote: he will worry for no reason. (P06, Phase 2, L63)
Reflexivity note: No logs establish alert accuracy.

Definition: Older adults compare reminders with prescriptions, medicine strips, notes, and established routines.
Sub-theme: People check before trusting the agent
Theme: Older adults accept family involvement when they stay in control
Example quote: The prescription is the authority for me. (P15, Phase 2, L43)
Reflexivity note: Material records remain accountable references, not automatically error free.

Definition: Older adults reject duplicate, unfamiliar, or contradictory medication instructions.
Sub-theme: People check before trusting the agent
Theme: Older adults accept family involvement when they stay in control
Example quote: I will not take another one just because the app says so. (P05, Phase 2, L43)
Reflexivity note: The elicited veto expresses a clear authority boundary.

Definition: Older adults and relatives compare names and timings before relying on routine reminders.
Sub-theme: People check before trusting the agent
Theme: Older adults accept family involvement when they stay in control
Example quote: My son checked it first. I also watched what it was saying. (P04, Phase 2, L145)
Reflexivity note: This is lived checking, not the unimplemented probationary mode.

Definition: Repeated reminders make dose times easier to anticipate without replacing established memory or routines.
Sub-theme: Reminders can strengthen an existing routine
Theme: The agent helps when it supports routines and shows uncertainty
Example quote: Maybe it has reinforced the timing. (P11, Phase 2, L110)
Reflexivity note: Elicited by a leading prompt but retained because the response rejects memory replacement.

Definition: Notes, prescriptions, habits, recognition, and human reminders remain available if the agent stops.
Sub-theme: Reminders can strengthen an existing routine
Theme: The agent helps when it supports routines and shows uncertainty
Example quote: My notes are working well for me. The reminder is just extra help. (P16, Phase 2, L141)
Reflexivity note: Retained competence limits dependence claims.

Definition: Wrong content, repeated disturbance, or undisclosed action can end use.
Sub-theme: People check before trusting the agent
Theme: Older adults accept family involvement when they stay in control
Example quote: Wrong medicine, wrong timing, too many alerts. If it changes something without telling us, also bad. (P04, Phase 2, L193)
Reflexivity note: These are hypothetical stopping conditions.

Definition: Longstanding medication routines exist before any streak or score is introduced.
Sub-theme: Routines and prescriptions come before scores
Theme: Routines and prescriptions matter more than scores and streaks
Example quote: I don't need a score to take my medicines. I have been doing this for eighteen years. (P11, Phase 2, L84)
Reflexivity note: This account directly limits gamification as a primary motive.

Definition: Following a clinician's prescription provides a reason for taking medicine independent of points.
Sub-theme: Routines and prescriptions come before scores
Theme: Routines and prescriptions matter more than scores and streaks
Example quote: I don't take medicine because of the points. I take it because the doctor prescribed it. (P15, Phase 2, L103)
Reflexivity note: The participant distinguishes obligation from game feedback.

Definition: Some older adults find scores unnecessary or difficult to interpret within established routines.
Sub-theme: Routines and prescriptions come before scores
Theme: Routines and prescriptions matter more than scores and streaks
Example quote: I don't understand these scores very much. (P09, Phase 2, L82)
Reflexivity note: Unfamiliarity challenges assumptions imported from younger users.

Code: A streak can add small interest
Definition: Visible continuity can add interest or a desire not to lose accumulated progress.
Sub-theme: A streak can add small interest
Theme: Routines and prescriptions matter more than scores and streaks
Example quote: when you see that you have been regular for many days, you don't want to lose it. (P05, Phase 2, L111)
Reflexivity note: The same account names habit as the main reason.

Definition: A streak gives involved relatives a way to notice sustained medication work.
Sub-theme: A streak can add small interest
Theme: Routines and prescriptions matter more than scores and streaks
Example quote: It became something they could see. But they don't need to make a big thing about it. (P07, Phase 2, L107)
Reflexivity note: Visibility is relational but not an adherence outcome.

Definition: Losing accumulated progress can cause disappointment despite its secondary medical importance.
Sub-theme: Broken streaks can create pressure
Theme: Routines and prescriptions matter more than scores and streaks
Example quote: I was a little upset because I had kept it for many days. (P10, Phase 2, L79)
Reflexivity note: Streak grief is retained as a negative case.

Definition: Relatives redirect attention from lost progress to the next medication event.
Sub-theme: Broken streaks can create pressure
Theme: Routines and prescriptions matter more than scores and streaks
Example quote: my son said, okay, it happened, take the next one properly. (P10, Phase 2, L79)
Reflexivity note: Family response, not the score, contains metric distress.

Definition: Participants evaluate the medication event before points, numbers, or streak continuity.
Sub-theme: Broken streaks can create pressure
Theme: Routines and prescriptions matter more than scores and streaks
Example quote: Medicine is more important than the score. (P09, Phase 2, L90)
Reflexivity note: Points and shared scores were not deployed.

Definition: Monitoring, competition, or inflated attention makes the score unacceptable.
Sub-theme: Broken streaks can create pressure
Theme: Routines and prescriptions matter more than scores and streaks
Example quote: If it becomes another performance measure, then no. (P11, Phase 2, L92)
Reflexivity note: This countercase limits the coach role.

Definition: Older adults remind and check others as well as receive care themselves.
Sub-theme: People remind and learn from each other
Theme: Friends and community shape care, but doctors decide medicine
Example quote: I also ask her about her medicine. So it is both ways. (P06, Phase 2, L79)
Reflexivity note: Reciprocity resists casting older adults only as care recipients.

Definition: Hearing peers discuss medicines can redirect attention to one's own routine.
Sub-theme: People remind and learn from each other
Theme: Friends and community shape care, but doctors decide medicine
Example quote: If someone says they have to take their tablet, sometimes I remember mine. (P04, Phase 2, L241)
Reflexivity note: The community account was elicited from a subset.

Definition: Use by known peers can make unfamiliar technology appear more trustworthy.
Sub-theme: Community advice leads to questions, not decisions
Theme: Friends and community shape care, but doctors decide medicine
Example quote: If other farmers use it and say it works, I will trust it more. (P06, Phase 2, L199)
Reflexivity note: Social proof concerns adoption, not system accuracy.

Definition: Other people's medicine experiences can prompt consultation without authorizing a treatment change.
Sub-theme: Community advice leads to questions, not decisions
Theme: Friends and community shape care, but doctors decide medicine
Example quote: If many people are saying something, I may ask the doctor about it. But asking is different from taking it. (P15, Phase 2, L191)
Reflexivity note: This is elicited reasoning, not observed consultation.

Definition: Conflicting medicine stories can burden older adults rather than support care.
Sub-theme: Community advice leads to questions, not decisions
Theme: Friends and community shape care, but doctors decide medicine
Example quote: I listen, but I don't want the phone adding more confusion. (P07, Phase 2, L195)
Reflexivity note: Community connection is not assumed beneficial.

Definition: Conversational health sharing does not imply permission for automatic digital disclosure.
Sub-theme: Community advice leads to questions, not decisions
Theme: Friends and community shape care, but doctors decide medicine
Example quote: Family can see, other people don't need to. (P04, Phase 2, L137)
Reflexivity note: This refusal distinguishes sociality from unrestricted data access.

Definition: Spoken Bangla reaches users who do not monitor notifications or read small text.
Sub-theme: Simple prompts support direct use
Theme: The agent helps when it supports routines and shows uncertainty
Example quote: I don't have to read small writing. (P08, Phase 2, L217)
Reflexivity note: Spoken service announcements were deployed; voice reminder preferences were elicited.

Code: Images and plain Bangla support matching
Definition: Medicine images, large text, and familiar language connect prompts to known medicine.
Sub-theme: Simple prompts support direct use
Theme: The agent helps when it supports routines and shows uncertainty
Example quote: If it shows the packet, I can compare. (P08, Phase 2, L233)
Reflexivity note: Images were not deployed.

Definition: Few controls and concise prompts keep the agent understandable and bounded.
Sub-theme: Simple prompts support direct use
Theme: The agent helps when it supports routines and shows uncertainty
Example quote: The phone should remind, not decide. (P06, Phase 2, L235)
Reflexivity note: Complexity and authority are linked in this account.

Definition: A relative configures schedules while the older adult hears, recognizes, confirms, and acts.
Sub-theme: Family setup can preserve older adult control
Theme: Care tasks are divided while older adults stay involved
Example quote: My daughter set it up for me. After that, the reminder part was easy. (P05, Phase 2, L7)
Reflexivity note: Setup help is not treated as nonuse.

Definition: Configuration or supply help does not necessarily transfer the medication action.
Sub-theme: Family setup can preserve older adult control
Theme: Care tasks are divided while older adults stay involved
Example quote: I don't need someone to put it in my hand. I can take it myself. (P08, Phase 2, L185)
Reflexivity note: This protects task specific agency.

Definition: Portable prompts cover travel, fieldwork, gatherings, and altered routines where household cues recede.
Sub-theme: Reminders can strengthen an existing routine
Theme: The agent helps when it supports routines and shows uncertainty
Example quote: At home my wife can tell me. In the field there is nobody asking. (P06, Phase 2, L179)
Reflexivity note: This is reported value, not an adherence outcome.

Definition: Proposed low supply notices reach the person who obtains medicine.
Sub-theme: Features send tasks to responsible people
Theme: Care tasks are divided while older adults stay involved
Example quote: If my son gets a message before that, he can buy. (P06, Phase 2, L187)
Reflexivity note: Stock sensing was not deployed.

Definition: Proposed photo capture distributes interpretation only when people verify the extracted instruction.
Sub-theme: Features send tasks to responsible people
Theme: Care tasks are divided while older adults stay involved
Example quote: If there is doubt, we ask the doctor or pharmacy. (P04, Phase 2, L221)
Reflexivity note: Prescription capture was not implemented.
